beats.narration: Begin by framing Introduction to Cooperative Education as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results. Cooperative education is a work experience designed to supplement the educational process. Consider this worked case: Students complete a semester-long software development project at a local tech firm while maintaining full-time coursework. On screen, display a split-screen graphic showing a classroom lecture on the left and a student coding in a corporate office on the right, with a central arrow labeled 'Supplementing Education'. List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion. This establishes the vocabulary and scope needed for the remaining sections.
beats.title: Introduction to Cooperative Education
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a split-screen graphic showing a classroom lecture on the left and a student coding in a corporate office on the right, with a central arrow labeled 'Supplementing Education'.

beats.narration: Now define Part-Time Structure and Scheduling precisely enough that another learner could test the definition. Activities are done on a part-time basis. Consider this worked case: The co-op schedule allocates approximately 15 hours per week, equivalent to one full-time course credit, allowing students to attend lectures and complete assignments. On screen, show a weekly timeline calendar highlighting 15 hours of co-op work distributed across weekdays, with academic classes marked separately. Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them. A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise.
beats.title: Part-Time Structure and Scheduling
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a weekly timeline calendar highlighting 15 hours of co-op work distributed across weekdays, with academic classes marked separately.

beats.narration: With the foundation in place, examine how Prerequisite Requirements operates in a concrete sequence. They should respect privacy. Consider this worked case: A freshman student who has not yet taken an introductory programming course must take CSCI-099 in the preceding semester to qualify for the co-op program. On screen, create a prerequisite flowchart showing CSCI-099 as a required gateway node before the CSCI-399 co-op course node. Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition. The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Prerequisite Requirements
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Create a prerequisite flowchart showing CSCI-099 as a required gateway node before the CSCI-399 co-op course node.

beats.narration: Next, compare the choices involved in Term Offerings and make the decision criteria explicit. They should honor confidentiality. Consider this worked case: Students can enroll in the co-op program during any of these three academic terms, providing flexibility to align work experience with career goals. On screen, list the three terms (Fall, Spring, Summer) as horizontal buttons with checkmarks, indicating availability for co-op enrollment. Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts. Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Term Offerings
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | List the three terms (Fall, Spring, Summer) as horizontal buttons with checkmarks, indicating availability for co-op enrollment.

beats.narration: Apply Ethical Foundations in Co-op to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition. The ACM Code directs computing professionals to contribute to society and human well-being. Consider this worked case: A co-op student developing a healthcare app must ensure the system does not compromise patient data privacy or cause unintended harm to users. On screen, display a shield icon with three sub-icons representing 'Contribute to Society', 'Avoid Harm', and 'Human Well-being'. Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step. The worked case shows both how to apply the method and how to check it.
beats.title: Ethical Foundations in Co-op
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a shield icon with three sub-icons representing 'Contribute to Society', 'Avoid Harm', and 'Human Well-being'.

beats.narration: Examine the tradeoffs in Honesty and Trustworthiness, including what improves and what becomes more difficult. They should be honest and trustworthy. Consider this worked case: When documenting co-op progress, students must accurately report completed tasks and challenges without exaggerating results or omitting critical failures. On screen, show a checklist graphic with items like 'Accurate Reporting', 'Transparent Documentation', and 'Trustworthy Updates' next to a co-op project dashboard. State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable. Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Honesty and Trustworthiness
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a checklist graphic with items like 'Accurate Reporting', 'Transparent Documentation', and 'Trustworthy Updates' next to a co-op project dashboard.

beats.narration: Stress-test the reasoning around Fairness and Non-Discrimination with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome. They should be fair and take action not to discriminate. Consider this worked case: A co-op team must ensure equitable distribution of tasks and recognition among all members, regardless of background or role. On screen, illustrate a balanced scale with 'Equitable Task Distribution' on one side and 'Inclusive Recognition' on the other, labeled 'Fairness in Co-op Teams'. Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds. The edge case reveals the boundary of the claim without discarding the useful core idea.
beats.title: Fairness and Non-Discrimination
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Illustrate a balanced scale with 'Equitable Task Distribution' on one side and 'Inclusive Recognition' on the other, labeled 'Fairness in Co-op Teams'.

beats.narration: Use Responsible Technical Communication to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action. Responsible technical communication distinguishes claims from evidence. Consider this worked case: When presenting co-op findings, students must clearly separate their own contributions from existing research and provide proper citations for all referenced methods. On screen, show a document template with sections labeled 'Claim', 'Evidence', 'Prior Work', and 'Contribution', demonstrating proper structure. Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause. The diagnosis is strongest when another person can reproduce the observation and the test.
beats.title: Responsible Technical Communication
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a document template with sections labeled 'Claim', 'Evidence', 'Prior Work', and 'Contribution', demonstrating proper structure.

beats.narration: Connect Research Integrity and Evaluation to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system. Authors should preserve research integrity and avoid plagiarism, fabrication, and falsification. Consider this worked case: Co-op students must verify all data sources, accurately report limitations, and never alter results to fit a desired conclusion. On screen, create a flowchart showing 'Data Collection' -> 'Verification' -> 'Accurate Reporting' -> 'Limitations Disclosed', with red X marks over 'Fabrication' and 'Falsification'. Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations. The synthesis matters only if every connection remains supported by the original evidence.
beats.title: Research Integrity and Evaluation
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Create a flowchart showing 'Data Collection' -> 'Verification' -> 'Accurate Reporting' -> 'Limitations Disclosed', with red X marks over 'Fabrication' and 'Falsification'.

beats.narration: Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis. They should maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice. Consider this worked case: Before submitting a co-op project, students check that they have identified stakeholders, documented methods for reproducibility, and verified all claims against evidence. On screen, display a printable checklist with boxes for 'Ethical Review Complete', 'Communication Standards Met', 'Evaluation Criteria Applied', and 'Sources Cited'. For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step. The result is a repeatable procedure, not a conclusion that depends on memory or intuition.
beats.title: Practical Analysis Checklist
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a printable checklist with boxes for 'Ethical Review Complete', 'Communication Standards Met', 'Evaluation Criteria Applied', and 'Sources Cited'.

claims.text: Cooperative education is a work experience designed to supplement the educational process.
Activities are done on a part-time basis.
The ACM Code directs computing professionals to contribute to society and human well-being.
They should be honest and trustworthy.
They should be fair and take action not to discriminate.
Responsible technical communication distinguishes claims from evidence.
Authors should preserve research integrity and avoid plagiarism, fabrication, and falsification.
They should maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice.

sources.author: Rochester Institute of Technology
sources.excerpt: Cooperative education is a work experience designed to supplement the educational process. Students may select from a range of activities designated as cooperative education as described by their program of study. Activities are done on a part-time basis. Prerequisite: CSCI-099 or equivalent course. Typically Offered: Fall, Spring, Summer
sources.title: RIT CSCI-399 CS Undergraduate Part-time Co-op catalog description

sources.author: Association for Computing Machinery
sources.excerpt: The ACM Code directs computing professionals to contribute to society and human well-being. Computing professionals should avoid harm. They should be honest and trustworthy. They should be fair and take action not to discriminate. They should respect the work required to produce new ideas and creative works. They should respect privacy. They should honor confidentiality. Professionals should strive to achieve high quality in both processes and products. They should maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice. Robust security should be designed and implemented when appropriate. Ethical computing decisions identify stakeholders, foreseeable benefits and harms, uncertainty, alternatives, and obligations.
sources.title: ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct

sources.author: Association for Computing Machinery
sources.excerpt: Responsible technical communication distinguishes claims from evidence. It cites prior work and identifies the contribution being reported. Methods should be described well enough for readers to evaluate the work. Results should be reported accurately rather than selected to create a misleading conclusion. Limitations and threats to validity should be made visible. Authors should preserve research integrity and avoid plagiarism, fabrication, and falsification. Conflicts and relevant relationships should be disclosed according to publication policy. A research project narrows a question, reviews literature, defines a reproducible method, evaluates results, and communicates for the intended audience.
sources.title: ACM Publications Policies
